title: Microsoft Purview: Priority cleanup to permanently delete Exchange mailbox items under holds (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, controls, licensing and deletion safeguards are supported. Add the Worldwide roadmap citation and acknowledge that the Exchange documentation gives conflicting descriptions of when all three approvals are required.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Priority cleanup for the Exchange workload in Data Lifecycle Management.
claims.quote: Data Lifecycle Management - Introduction of secure workflow to bypass legal holds and retention policies in Exchange

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a recurring exception to delete items under a broader retention policy or legal hold.
claims.quote: The first release of Priority cleanup enables admins to create a recurring exception to delete items under a broader retention policy and/or legal hold on Exchange workload.

claims.claim: Creating a Priority cleanup requires a separate security role.
claims.quote: Creating a Priority cleanup will require a separate security role

claims.claim: Creating a Priority cleanup requires multiple approvers.
claims.quote: Creating a Priority cleanup will require a separate security role, multiple approvers

claims.claim: The roadmap promises a complete audit trail.
claims.quote: and will have a complete audit trail

claims.where: front matter: clouds; title; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Web as the platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record has no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: Learn documents Exchange Priority cleanup as rolling out in preview and subject to change.
claims.quote: Priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and subject to change.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The Exchange Learn page does not identify the clouds its feature description covers.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "GCC" "default"; read priority-cleanup-exchange in full and government-cloud search results; no cloud-specific scope statement found.

claims.claim: The policy uses a Keyword Query Language search query over mailboxes.
claims.quote: enter text into the KeyQL editor box to construct a query using Exchange email properties

claims.claim: The administrator can choose deletion as soon as possible or after retaining items for a specified period.
claims.quote: choose whether to permanently delete the matched items as soon as possible or retain them for a specific period and then delete them

claims.claim: The policy configuration names approvers.
claims.quote: For the Assign who'll approve what gets deleted page, this is where you need to specify another priority cleanup approver

claims.claim: Items follow the normal retention deletion process and timings.
claims.quote: Items still go through the same deletion process with the same timings to ensure a compliant permanent deletion

claims.claim: Priority cleanup does not require waiting for the retention period to expire or the hold to be released.
claims.quote: there's no need to wait for the retention period to expire or the hold to be released

claims.claim: Simulation mode allows review of returned samples.
claims.quote: priority cleanup supports simulation, so you can check the returned samples in case the policy configuration needs any fine-tuning

claims.claim: Simulation for Exchange is recommended but not required.
claims.quote: Simulation required before running the policy: | No (but recommended) | Yes

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete items marked as records or regulatory records.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete data already copied into an eDiscovery review set.
claims.quote: the data might already be copied to an eDiscovery review set where it can't be deleted by priority cleanup

claims.claim: Roadmap item 392838 describes the same Exchange Priority cleanup feature for Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: 392838: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]; "The first release of Priority cleanup enables admins to create a recurring exception ... on Exchange workload."
claims.fix: Add https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/roadmap?id=392838 to sources as kind roadmap, titled Microsoft 365 Roadmap 392838; it supports the Worldwide item, target and preview date.

claims.claim: The Worldwide item targets January CY2027.
claims.quote: 392838: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The Worldwide item lists a preview date of February CY2025.
claims.quote: 392838: "previewDate": "February CY2025"

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Priority cleanup can override existing holds and Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: the deletion is irreversible and can override existing holds and even Preservation Lock

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After all required approvals, deletion is permanent and users, administrators and Microsoft cannot restore items.
claims.quote: When all the required approvals are complete, items are permanently deleted and cannot be restored by users, by admins, or by Microsoft.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists data spillage and privacy requests as use cases.
claims.quote: Privacy request: You receive a request to remove personal information ... Data spillage: An employee accidentally emailed sensitive information

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a default specifically for the government-cloud rollout, so the briefing uses unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "GCC" "default"; read roadmap 473493 and priority-cleanup-exchange; the record has no default and Learn gives no government-cloud rollout qualification.

claims.claim: The Exchange Learn page says the feature is enabled by default at tenant level.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: No source states that existing retention behaviour changes on arrival of this rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: Priority cleanup Exchange tenant configuration disable PowerShell Set PriorityCleanupEnabled GCC GCC High DoD default pricing meter; read roadmap 473493 and priority-cleanup-exchange; neither states an automatic change to existing retention.

claims.claim: Deleting a policy after approval completes may still leave its items to be permanently deleted.
claims.quote: Although you can delete a priority cleanup policy, if the approval process for it is complete, items might still be permanently deleted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn requires three approvals for every item: a priority cleanup admin, a retention manager and an eDiscovery admin.
claims.quote: Three approvals are always required, irrespective of which type of hold is applied to the item: One priority cleanup admin approval. One retention manager approval. One eDiscovery admin approval.
claims.fix: After this statement add: 'The same Learn page's approval-process section instead describes retention-manager approval as conditional on retention settings and eDiscovery-admin approval as conditional on an eDiscovery hold; confirm the actual workflow before use.'

claims.claim: Review-set data is automatically deleted when the entire eDiscovery case is deleted.
claims.quote: This data is automatically deleted when the entire eDiscovery case is deleted by an eDiscovery admin.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is required to create policies, enable or disable the feature and approve the initial stage.
claims.quote: This role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, enable or disable the feature, or approve items within the initial approval stage.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: First-stage approvers need Priority Cleanup Admin, Data Classification Content Viewer, Data Classification List Viewer and Disposition Management.
claims.quote: Priority cleanup admins | - Priority Cleanup admin- Data Classification Content Viewer- Data Classification List Viewer- Disposition Management

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is automatically added to Organization Management only and must be added manually to other role groups.
claims.quote: This role is automatically added to the Organization Management role group but must be manually added to any other role group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The first-stage approver should differ from the creator, but Learn says this is not enforced.
claims.quote: This should be a different person to the user who created the priority cleanup policy, but isn't enforced.

claims.claim: Approvers must be individual users; mail-enabled security groups are not supported.
claims.quote: Approvers must be individual users. Mail-enabled security groups are not currently supported.

claims.claim: Applying an enabled policy to items and triggering approval can take up to seven days.
claims.quote: it can take up to seven days to apply the policy to items and trigger the approval process

claims.claim: Permanent deletion of approved items can take up to seven days.
claims.quote: Allow up to seven days for items to be permanently deleted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn describes typical Exchange policy use as Rare.
claims.quote: Typical policy use: | Rare

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Identified emails display an Outlook Retention message bar with the policy name and (-1 days).
claims.quote: users see a Retention: message bar on their emails in Outlook when they're identified for priority cleanup. They also see the name of the priority cleanup policy, then (-1 days)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[4].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: PriorityCleanupTagApplied and PriorityCleanupDelete are mailbox cleanup audit operations without portal friendly names.
claims.quote: Operation name of PriorityCleanupTagApplied ... Operation name of PriorityCleanupDelete ... Currently, these events don't have friendly names to select from the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Entitlement has mixed licensed routes, including suite licences and Information Protection and Governance licences.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5; Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW; Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW; Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance; Office 365 E5/A5/G5

claims.where: Cost and licensing; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The listed Microsoft 365, Office 365, Purview Suite, Defender + Purview Suite FLW and Information Protection and Governance licences provide Priority cleanup user rights.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5; Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW; Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW; Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance; Office 365 E5/A5/G5

claims.claim: Every user benefiting from the service requires a licence.
claims.quote: Any user benefiting from the service requires a license.

claims.claim: Users assigned a Purview role for portal use are among those requiring a licence.
claims.quote: Users with a Purview role assigned for use in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Users associated with Exchange user mailboxes need the required licence when a Purview policy or feature is used there.
claims.quote: Exchange user mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, Teams chats, and devices are associated with a user account, so the user must have the required license assigned when a Purview policy or feature is used in these locations.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No feature-specific meter, price or storage charge is documented in the feature page or service description.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "price" "meter" licensing; read priority-cleanup-exchange and searched microsoft-purview-service-description for Priority cleanup, price, meter and storage charge; no cleanup-specific charge found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Each reviewer's required roles must be assigned before creation, or policy creation fails.
claims.quote: The approver at each stage of the review process must have the correct roles assigned before the policy can be created. ... If the reviewer at any stage doesn't have the correct roles assigned in advance, policy creation fails with an error.

claims.claim: Auditing must be enabled at least one day before creating and running the first policy.
claims.quote: Make sure that auditing is enabled at least one day before you create and run the first priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: A mailbox requires at least 10 MB of data to support Priority cleanup.
claims.quote: A mailbox must have at least 10-MB data to support priority cleanup.

claims.claim: Group mailboxes are supported only through adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Group mailboxes are supported via adaptive scopes only.

claims.claim: The tenant-level switch covers Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for SharePoint and OneDrive as well as for Exchange.

claims.claim: One cleanup policy cannot cover all three workloads.
claims.quote: you can't create a cleanup policy for all three locations in same policy

claims.claim: The Purview role-group page supports security groups only in commercial-cloud organisations.
claims.quote: Security groups are supported only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organizations.

claims.claim: The tenant switch is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management. ... select Priority cleanup settings. ... From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell setting for the tenant-wide switch is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "tenant" "PowerShell" disable configuration; PriorityCleanupEnabled GCC GCC High DoD; read Exchange switch instructions and PowerShell search results; found policy/label operations, not a tenant-wide switch.

claims.claim: Policy creation starts at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup, and then select + Create a priority cleanup.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -PriorityCleanup to create a Priority cleanup policy.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... The PriorityCleanup switch specifies whether to create a Priority cleanup policy. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.

claims.claim: The printed Purview Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups route reaches Choose users for editing a built-in role group's membership.
claims.quote: Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" grants the role group's permissions to the selected user.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: When auditing is off, Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity enables auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. ... Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search is the audit search route.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog searches the audit log using Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: you can use this cmdlet to search the audit log instead of using the search tool on the Audit page in the Microsoft Purview portal. You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs is required for audit search.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. ... To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Existing priority cleanup policies continue running after the tenant control is disabled.
claims.quote: If priority cleanup policies are already created when you turn off the control: Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function

claims.claim: Existing policies remain deletable after the tenant control is disabled.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted

claims.claim: Existing policies cannot be modified after the tenant control is disabled.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can't be modified

claims.claim: Retention approvers need Retention Management, Data Classification Content Viewer, Data Classification List Viewer and Disposition Management.
claims.quote: Retention managers | - Retention Management- Data Classification Content Viewer- Data Classification List Viewer- Disposition Management

claims.claim: The detailed eDiscovery approver requirements list Search And Purge, Hold, Review, Data Classification Content Viewer, Data Classification List Viewer and Disposition Management.
claims.quote: eDiscovery admins | - Search And Purge- Hold- Review- Data Classification Content Viewer- Data Classification List Viewer- Disposition Management

claims.claim: The policy-wizard instructions name eDiscovery Administrator for the eDiscovery stage.
claims.quote: eDiscovery admins: Must be assigned the eDiscovery Administrator role.

claims.claim: The portal displays a Cleanup ID after policy creation.
claims.quote: On the Your priority cleanup policy has been created page, you see the Cleanup ID that's used to track and monitor this policy.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Governance guidance; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The cleanup ID can be used as an audit keyword search term to monitor the policy.
claims.quote: Use the details of a policy to identify its cleanup ID, and paste this number as a keyword search string from the auditing solution.

claims.claim: Learn suggests highly regulated organisations using Preservation Lock may want to disable priority cleanup at tenant level.
claims.quote: highly regulated organizations that use Preservation Lock might want the additional safeguard of turning off priority cleanup at the tenant level to ensure that their policies remain in compliance with required regulations

claims.claim: The tenant-level control is the only documented switch for stopping creation of new policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "tenant" "PowerShell" disable configuration; read priority-cleanup-exchange and tenant-switch search results; no other switch for stopping new-policy creation was documented.

claims.claim: The New-RetentionCompliancePolicy reference does not describe the Exchange approver steps.
claims.quote: Searched: new-retentioncompliancepolicy reference text for approv, eDiscovery Administrator and Retention Management; no matches. Read its PriorityCleanup parameter description.

claims.claim: Disabling the tenant control prevents new priority cleanup policies from being created until it is enabled again.
claims.quote: New priority cleanup policies can't be created until you turn on the control and select Save again.
